name: Pencil
description: A self-hosted feedback-to-action loop for one business: ask a short adaptive flow, surface evidence, and own the next action.
scope: One business, one shared workspace, equal operators with no roles.

capabilities.description: The owner-configured public landing at `/`, matching the canonical published flow's respondent experience and admission state.

Pencil's own product page at `/` by default (`/pencil` redirects there) and documentation at `/docs`: sessionless, cookieless and same-origin. An explicit respondent landing selection overrides the default root.
A session-gated operator shell at `/app` with labelled, keyboard-operable navigation; `/signin` is the only sessionless entry point.
Equal operators with no roles, invited and removed in settings, whose sign-in depends on mail.
One workspace time zone and sending-hours window, plus the guarantee that optional AI and task adapters are configuration, not degradation.
An onboarding empty state and a sortable flow list with completion and audience figures.
Building, branching, validating, publishing, and revising adaptive flows with stable structure IDs.
Contacts, segments, and participants for inviting a known audience with consent and send-time eligibility checks.
Public links, embeds, invitations, reminders, opt-out, and durable mail delivery with retry and adapter isolation.
The one-question-at-a-time public flow: answers, back navigation, privacy disclosure, abuse defences, and quarantine review.
A response ledger with filters, counts, and lossless CSV/JSON export.
AI-free response summary, drop-off, stated denominators, device split, and cross-revision results.
Budgeted, evidence-linked AI analysis with disclosure thresholds, provenance, output validation, and visible failure.
Turning a recommendation, written by an operator or later by an analysis, into an owned, measurable action with idempotent, confirmed external task delivery.
Implemented per-flow Immediately or Off response mail with durable delivery state and no mail loops. The notification centre and daily digests remain deferred.
Complete export and bounded response erasure across every dependent record.
Saved business name, supporting line, accessible accent, own-origin logo and public landing selection across respondent surfaces.
Reviewed form-definition and historical response imports with explicit losses, resumable inert commits and guarded undo.

nonGoals: Video, audio, signature, and file-upload questions
Storing or reporting the answers of an abandoned session

externals.why: Cloudflare has no owned primitive that delivers transactional email to external recipients, and BASE-ACCESS-001 magic-link sign-in is delivered by mail, so no deployment can run without it.
data: operator email and magic-link sign-in token
invitation, reminder, notification, or digest copy

externals.why: Evidence synthesis and draft-question assistance require a model provider; no model is bundled with the deployment.
data: draft question text for requested assistance
completed answer text and structured values selected for an analysis
stable response IDs without contact identity

externals.why: Creating a task in a buyer-selected task system necessarily sends the confirmed action to that system.

env.name: APP_ORIGIN
env.why: Canonical HTTPS origin for auth, reports, and public flow links.

env.name: PENCIL_BUILD_ID
env.why: Exact deploy candidate identifier shown by `/health` after its D1 readiness check.

env.name: MAIL_PROVIDER
env.why: Selects the mail sender adapter. Required: magic-link sign-in depends on it (OPER-003).

env.name: MAIL_API_KEY
env.why: Authenticates transactional sign-in, invitation, reminder, and notification mail.

env.name: MAIL_FROM
env.why: Verified no-reply sender address used for every outbound message (NOTIFY-004).

env.name: AI_PROVIDER
env.why: Selects the optional AI adapter; when absent ANLY-008 and WS-003 apply.

env.name: AI_MODEL
env.why: Model required when AI analysis or assistance is enabled.

env.name: AI_API_KEY
env.why: Authenticates the configured AI provider when AI is enabled.

env.name: TASK_PROVIDER
env.why: Selects the optional task destination adapter; webhook is the only one included. When absent ACT-004 and WS-003 apply.

env.name: TASK_WEBHOOK_URL
env.why: The https endpoint of the deployer's task system for TASK_PROVIDER=webhook; it must create or return one task per idempotency key (docs/guide/actions.md).

env.name: TASK_API_KEY
env.why: Authenticates the optional task destination; sent only as a bearer value and never stored, logged or exported.

env.name: SESSION_SECRET
env.why: At least 32 random bytes encoded for Base HMAC session and one-time token hashes; preserve across restarts.

env.name: SETUP_TOKEN
env.why: Independent one-time bootstrap secret required only until the first Base operator is established. Remove after setup; the durable ledger forbids a second bootstrap.

deploy.notes: `/` matches only the literal root document, never as a prefix over the whole deployment: a matcher must compare `/` for exact equality, not `path.startsWith('/')`, which would trivially admit every route. Every other entry ending in `/` is a true prefix — `/f/` for direct flow links, `/embed/` for the embed script, `/auth/` for the sign-in flow, `/assets/` for static files, `/api/public/` for unauthenticated public API reads — and covers everything under it. Every other entry is one exact, sessionless document. Everything else, including the rest of `/app` and `/api/`, requires an operator or respondent session. Start owns generated /_serverFn/ transport; each private handler independently validates the native operator session. /__dev/outbox is available only in explicitly configured loopback development; deployed environments return 404. `/` is the default Pencil product page (or the explicitly selected respondent landing); `/pencil` redirects to `/` and `/docs` is the documentation home, all exact sessionless documents; `/docs/` is the prefix for documentation pages under it, so `/docs` is deliberately declared both exact and as the stem of that prefix. An explicitly selected respondent landing at `/` keeps its existing behavior.

limits.notes: These are design targets, not proven capacities. The backend pass must load-test them, revise the values, and mark status as tested before release.

operatingCost.workersPaidRequiredWhen: The first measured boundary is any of: the 100,001st dynamic Worker request in a UTC day; an invocation that cannot stay within the Free plan's 10 ms CPU limit; the 5,000,001st D1 row read or 100,001st D1 row written in a UTC day; one D1 database exceeding 500 MB or the account exceeding 5 GB; or the 10,001st Queue operation in a UTC day. A normally delivered Queue message consumes write, read, and delete operations, so 3,334 such messages cross the Queue boundary. The declared capacity targets are not Free-capable or load-tested and are not a monthly usage forecast.
excludes: R2 usage above its Standard free tier
operatingCost.assumptions: The current thin spine uses one Worker and D1. R2 and Queues are declared but not implemented; R2 Standard includes 10 GB-month storage, 1 million Class A operations, 10 million Class B operations, and free egress each month. No second worker, Durable Object, Workflow, KV, or hosted database is used until a measured need exists.
